spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Lambda architecture forces teams to write and reconcile two separate codebases (e.g., Spark SQL for batch + Flink for real-time), guaranteeing semantic drift between yesterday's dashboard and today's.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Immutable Kafka Log (Live + Tiered S3) -> Flink v1/v2 -> Atomic View Swap (Kafka + Tiered S3 Log -> Flink Stream Job v2 -> Serving Table v1 -> Serving Table v2); Zero-Downtime Offset-0 Backfill & Serving Alias Swap (Kafka + S3 Tiered -> Flink job-v2 -> Serving view_v2 -> Query Alias).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Explore late-data watermarking, Kafka exactly-once fencing, and how Kappa contrasts with Lambda. Replaying 30 days of Kafka events at 500k events/sec will DDoS your serving database if written live.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore late-data watermarking, Kafka exactly-once fencing, and how Kappa contrasts with Lambda.

learningJourney.title: What is Kappa Architecture

explanation.foundation: Lambda architecture forces teams to write and reconcile two separate codebases (e.g., Spark SQL for batch + Flink for real-time), guaranteeing semantic drift between yesterday's dashboard and today's. **Kappa Architecture** (Jay Kreps) deletes the batch layer.
explanation.core: An immutable partitioned log (**Kafka** with `retention.ms=-1` or **Tiered Storage** to S3/GCS, or **Apache Pulsar**) is the **Single Source of Truth**. One stream codebase (Flink / Kafka Streams) handles both live tailing and historical backfills using **event-time watermarks**.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Kappa Stream-Only Architecture, watch how what is kappa architecture interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Kappa architecture eliminates the separate batch layer of Lambda architecture by treating an append-only distributed log as the single source of truth for both real-time processing and historical replay.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Kappa Stream-Only Architecture without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, one code path, one immutable log: when business logic changes, you spin up a second stream job from offset 0, backfill a new serving table, and atomically swap pointers.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Bounded RocksDB State TTL & Idempotent Watermark Config

explanation.foundation: Think of **Bounded RocksDB State TTL & Idempotent Watermark Config** as the intuition layer for Kappa Stream-Only Architecture: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.
explanation.core: Prevent unbounded RocksDB state growth by configuring `StateTtlConfig` on keyed descriptors and enabling incremental RocksDB checkpoints to S3.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, bounded rocksdb state ttl & idempotent watermark config becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Kappa architecture eliminates the separate batch layer of Lambda architecture by treating an append-only distributed log as the single source of truth for both real-time processing and historical replay.

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```java
// Flink StateTtlConfig + Idleness Watermark preventing RocksDB bloat & watermark stalls
StateTtlConfig ttlConfig = StateTtlConfig
    .newBuilder(Time.days(30))
    .setUpdateType(StateTtlConfig.UpdateType.OnCreateAndWrite)
    .setStateVisibility(StateTtlConfig.StateVisibility.NeverReturnExpired)
    .cleanupInRocksdbCompactFilter(1000)
    .build();

WatermarkStrategy<Event> wm = WatermarkStrategy
    .<Event>forBoundedOutOfOrderness(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .withTimestampAssigner((e, ts) -> e.eventTimeMs())
    .withIdleness(Duration.ofSeconds(30));
```

knowledgeCheck.question: Why can a single idle Kafka partition stall event-time window outputs across an entire Apache Flink Kappa pipeline?

options.text: Because Flink's global operator watermark advances to `min(partition_watermarks)`, so an idle partition holds the watermark back unless `withIdleness()` is configured
options.feedback: Correct: `WatermarkStrategy.withIdleness()` marks quiet partitions idle so active partitions keep advancing.

options.text: Because RocksDB locks all partitions until every partition receives 1,000 events
options.feedback: RocksDB state is keyed independently; the stall is due to watermark progression.

options.text: Because Kafka Tiered Storage deletes idle partitions
options.feedback: Tiered Storage only offloads old closed segments to object storage.
